identificationModule.briefTitle: Study of Radiotherapy Combined With Cisplatin/Carboplatin, Adebrelimab and Bevacizumab in the Treatment of TNBC-BM.
identificationModule.officialTitle: A Prospective, Two-arm, Multi-centre, Phase II Clinical Study of Radiotherapy Combined With Cisplatin/Carboplatin, Adebrelimab and Bevacizumab in the Treatment of Patients With Brain Metastasis From Triple-Negative Breast Cancer

descriptionModule.briefSummary: This is an open-label, prospective, two-arm, multicenter phase II clinical trial. The aim is to explore the efficacy and safety of radiotherapy combined with cisplatin/carboplatin, adebrelimab, and bevacizumab in patients with triple-negative breast cancer and brain metastases.

armGroups.label: Radiotherapy followed by systemic therapy group
armGroups.description: Patient who are eligible for inclusion will recieve radiotherapy first, followed by adebrelimab, bevacizumab and Cisplatin/Carplatin.

armGroups.label: Systemic therapy followed by radiotherapy group
armGroups.description: Patient who are eligible for inclusion will recieve adebrelimab, bevacizumab and Cisplatin/Carplatin followed by radiotherapy.

interventions.name: Radiation Therapy
interventions.description: Patients will receive either Fractionated Stereotactic Radiotherapy (FSRT) or Whole Brain Radiotherapy (WBRT), at the discretion of the treating physician based on the number, size, and location of brain metastases.

primaryOutcomes.description: The 12-month CNS-PFS rate was used for intracranial efficacy assessment based on RANO-BM, and extracranial efficacy assessment based on RECIST 1.1.

secondaryOutcomes.description: ntracranial objective response rate is defined as the proportion of patients who achieve a best overall intracranial response of complete response (CR) or partial response (PR), as assessed by RANO-BM criteria.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Up to 24 months(Efficacy assessments at 6 weeks post-treatment initiation, followed by every 9 weeks thereafter starting from Month 12)

secondaryOutcomes.description: Clinical benefit rate is defined as the proportion of patients who achieve a best overall intracranial response of complete response (CR), partial response (PR), or stable disease (SD) lasting for at least 24 weeks, as assessed by RANO-BM criteria.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Up to 24 months (Efficacy assessments at 6 weeks post-treatment initiation, followed by every 9 weeks thereafter starting from Month 12)

secondaryOutcomes.description: Objective response rate is defined as the proportion of patients who achieve a best overall response of complete response (CR) or partial response (PR)
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Up to 24 months (Efficacy assessments at 6 weeks post-treatment initiation, followed by every 9 weeks thereafter starting from Month 12)

secondaryOutcomes.description: clinical benefit rate is defined as the proportion of patients who achieve a best overall response of complete response (CR), partial response (PR), or stable disease (SD) lasting for at least 24 weeks.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Up to 24 months (Efficacy assessments at 6 weeks post-treatment initiation, followed by every 9 weeks thereafter starting from Month 12)

secondaryOutcomes.description: Duration of response is defined as the time from first documented objective response (CR or PR) until disease progression or death from any cause, whichever occurs first.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: From first documented response to progression or death, assessed up to 24 months

secondaryOutcomes.description: Intracranial progression-free survival is defined as the time from treatment initiation until intracranial disease progression per RANO-BM criteria or death from any cause, whichever occurs first.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: From randomization to intracranial progression or death, assessed up to 24 months.

secondaryOutcomes.description: Progression-free survival is defined as the time from treatment initiation to disease progression or death from any cause, whichever occurs first.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: From randomization to progression or death, assessed up to 24 months.

secondaryOutcomes.description: Overall survival is defined as the time from the start of treatment to death from any cause.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: From randomization to death, assessed up to 24 months.

secondaryOutcomes.description: Adverse events will be assessed and graded according to NCI-CTCAE version 5.0.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: From randomization through 30 days after the last dose of study treatment, assessed up to 24 months.

secondaryOutcomes.description: Neurocognitive function assessed using the Hopkins Verbal Learning Test-Revised (HVLT-R).
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: At screening, 12, 24, 36, 48 weeks, 1.5 years, and 2 years after radiotherapy completion

secondaryOutcomes.description: Quality of life assessed using the Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy-Brain (FACT-Br) questionnaire.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: At screening, within 3 days before each cycle of treatment, and at end of treatment or safety follow-up, assessed up to 24 months

secondaryOutcomes.description: Neurocognitive function assessed using the Animal Verbal Fluency Test.

secondaryOutcomes.description: Neurocognitive function assessed using the Trail Making Test (TMT-A/TMT-B)
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: At screening, 12, 24, 36, 48 weeks, 1.5 years, and 2 years after radiotherapy completion

secondaryOutcomes.description: Quality of life assessed using the EORTC Core Quality of Life Questionnaire (QLQ-C30), scoring from 0 to 100. This questionnaire is for functional and global quality of life scales, higher scores mean a better level of functioning. For symptom-oriented scales, a higher score means more severesymptoms.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: At screening, within 3 days before each cycle of treatment, and at end of treatment or safety follow-up, assessed up to 24 months

secondaryOutcomes.description: Quality of life assessed using the EORTC Quality of Life Questionnaire for Brain Neoplasms (QLQ-BN20). This aims to evaluate the effects of the tumour and its treatment on symptoms, functions and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) of brain tumour patients. The scale scoring form 0 to 100, and a higher score generally indicates more severe symptoms and poorer quality of life.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: At screening, within 3 days before each cycle of treatment, and at end of treatment or safety follow-up, assessed up to 24 months

otherOutcomes.description: Tumor tissue (≥10 unstained slides or fresh tissue specimens), blood (8 mL of clotted blood, 8 mL of anticoagulated blood), cerebrospinal fluid (8 mL), urine (20 mL ), and stool samples (5 g) will be collected for exploratory cytological and multi-omics analyses to identify biomarkers associated with treatment response and resistance to radiotherapy combined with systemic therapy.
otherOutcomes.timeFrame: At baseline, after Cycle 2 (each cycle is 21 days), and at disease progression or treatment discontinuation (up to 24 months)
